content.comment_body: I'm new to using [product_name] PLCs but have some experience with Click PLCs from another manufacturer. I'm seeking help for a project. I need to program the [product_name] to move 2 stepper motors 100 steps every 20 seconds. I'm using a [product_name] with 24V transistor outputs, together with SureStep microstep drivers and SureStep Nema 34 motors. Previously, I accomplished this with the Click PLC using the program shown in my attached image, but I'm having trouble converting this logic to work in [product_name] programming software. Any assistance with translating this to the [product_name] environment would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

Are you asking if you need to activate an output for 20 seconds and then deactivate it for 20 seconds, repeating the cycle? The ladder logic you shared looks like a flashing output. If that's the case, you could use an Asynchronous Pulse Generator as shown below. Apologies if I've misunderstood your requirements.
Sorry, I didn't explain well. Every 20 seconds, I want the stepper motors to complete 100 steps, which is equivalent to half a turn.
In my view, the [product_name] is not ideal for applications involving stepper motor control.

Thread closed since the question was posted twice. The other thread titled 'Using NC proximity switch to turn off motors' is published in the [product_name] - Software conference. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are attempting to control stepper motors using the [product_name] module with transistor outputs for specific step counts on a timed cycle. The main user struggles to adapt logic from another PLC platform to the [product_name] programming environment and is unsure how to achieve this step-based control. Another user suggests the [product_name] may not be well suited for stepper motor tasks, highlighting possible functional limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] and its programming software to provide straightforward, effective control of stepper motors with timed, precise step counts, similar to functionality available on alternative PLC platforms.
